Title: Maxwell Street in Chicago (Ill.)
Description: View of three children, two of whom are African American, and one white, seated on the running board of an automobile in the Maxwell Street area of Chicago (Ill.).

Title: Maxwell Street exhibition photographs
Description: Views of residents of Maxwell Street area of Chicago (Ill.) 1966-1983. Include buyers and sellers at the Maxwell Street market and goods for sale. Also includes unposed views of people dancing, singing, lounging on the streets.

Title: Maxwell Street photographs by Nathan Lerner
Description: Images composed by Mr. Lerner of people and scenes in the Maxwell Street market area of Chicago.

Title: The New Maxwell Street Market poster 1994
Description: Poster published by the City of Chicago Department of Consumer Services advertising the relocated Maxwell Street Market at Canal and Taylor Streets.
Photographer: City of Chicago Department of Consumer Services

Title: Photographs of Maxwell Street
Description: Primarily includes images of Maxwell Street Market in Chicago, (Ill). Many images of children playing and posing for pictures, African Americans and Hispanic Americans playing musical instruments, and shopping. Many images of street musicians, peddlers selling their goods, poor persons sitting or lying in the streets. Some images of women shopping, posing for pictures, or walking. Photos taken by Wilton ("Monty") La Montaine.

Title: Sol Sackheim slides of Maxwell Street neighborhood
Description: Street scenes and people buying and selling merchandise in the Maxwell Street neighborhood in Chicago (Ill.) on a sunny day in spring.

Title: Helen Osterman photographs of Maxwell Street
Description: Photographs made by Helen Osterman showing the Maxwell Street Market and used by her to help select paintings that she donated to Chicago Historical Society in 2003. Osterman regarded the Maxwell Street Market as a unique and long-standing Chicago institution threatened by urban development in the 1990s.

Title: [Clothing merchants selling goods along Maxwell Street]
Description: Image of clothing merchants selling goods along Maxwell Street in the Sunday market in the Chicago Jewish community located in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. Clothing is hanging from the awnings and piled on tables along the street.

Title: [Merchants and shoppers gathering along Maxwell Street]
Description: Elevated view of merchants and shoppers gathering along West Maxwell Street at the Sunday market in the Chicago Jewish community located in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. Vendor stalls are lining the curbside and horse drawn carts are stopped in the street.

Title: Photographs of Maxwell Street and Midway Airport
Description: Forty images of the Maxwell Street neighborhood taken by an unknown photographer on a single day in June 1952 (numbered 1 to 40). Includes views of commercial and evangelical religious activities, the built environment, and the diverse groups that populated and frequented the Maxwell Street market. Also present are 1947 interior views and exterior views of Municipal Airport (later called Midway Airport ) some showing airplanes on the runways; and a few aerial views of buildings in and near the Chicago Loop, such as the Chicago Daily News building, Butler Brothers building, and Union Station.

Photographs of Maxwell Street Market during its last season at original location
Description: Photographs by Dr. Steven Balkin, showing the last summer season at the original Maxwell Street Market. Images are primarily of vendors at their stands, shoppers, and street musicians playing instruments, photographer Jeffrey Fletcher, and images of Piano C. Red and his Flat Foot Boogie Band. Attached to photographs are excerpts from interviews with their subjects, describing personal experiences at the Maxwell Street Market. The color photographs in this collection include an image of the intersection of Halsted and Maxwell Streets in the evening, as well as close-up images of Darrel and Wayne, musicians who played with Piano C. Red.

Title: [Merchants and shoppers along Maxwell Street, sign on left for second-hand clothing]
Description: Elevated view of merchants and shoppers along Maxwell Street at the Sunday market in the Chicago Jewish community located in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. Horse-drawn carriages are driving in the street, and a sign hanging on the left side of the image reads: The Secondhand Paradise Clothing / Special Cleaning Repairing Pressing.

Title: [Merchants selling clothing and a group of men inspecting the goods on Maxwell Street]
Description: Image of merchants selling clothing and a group of men inspecting the goods on Maxwell Street at the Sunday market in the Chicago Jewish community located in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. Shoppers are walking on the sidewalk to the right of the image.

Title: [Sweatshop at 132 Maxwell Street, women and men sewing at various tables and sewing machines in a workroom]
Description: Image of women and men sewing at various tables and sewing machines in the workroom of a sweatshop at 132 Maxwell Street in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois.

Title: [Merchants and shoppers along Maxwell Street, a rack of men's suit coats is visible in foreground]
Description: Elevated view of the merchants and shoppers along Maxwell Street at the Sunday market in the Chicago Jewish community located in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. A rack of men's suit coats is prominently displayed in this image.

Title: [Katherine Kelley, Alderman James H. Lawley, and Frederick Rex buying vegetables, Maxwell Street market]
Description: Group portrait of Katherine Kelley, Alderman James H. Lawley, and Frederick Rex buying vegetables at the Maxwell Street market in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. A crowd is looking on. Lawley was alderman of the 14th Ward and served as chairman of the market commission, while Rex served as secretary of the commission. The Maxwell Street market served many immigrants in its community.

Title: [Walter Schwass, Roy Doll, and Captain Daniel Lynch standing in a room in the Maxwell Street police station]
Description: Three-quarter length portrait of Walter Schwass, Roy Doll, and Chicago Police Captain Daniel Lynch standing in the Maxwell Street police station at 943 West Maxwell Street in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. The man on the left side of the image is inspecting a shotgun.

Title: Nathan Lerner collection of visual materials
Description: Visual materials by or about Nathan Lerner relating to his career as a photographer, artist, educator, and inventor and to his personal life. He was associated with the New Bauhaus, the School of Design, and later the Institute of Design in Chicago (Ill.) for many years. Collection contains primarily original negatives and slides of his early photographic work, of his paintings, and of his design work, including his lightbox explorations. Most negatives are not represented by photoprints in this collection. Photoprints in the collection are primarily family snapshots made in the United States, Japan, Mexico, or Europe and contact sheets, clippings from contact sheets, and other work prints. Also present are index cards (3 x 5 in.) by Lerner cataloging dates and locations for many of his photographs; exhibition posters for some of his exhibits, films, and videos; and films and videos about his work.

Title: Betty Ross-Rubin photograph collection
Description: Includes 2 photographs of the Maxwell Street area in 1938 and 20 photographic proof sheets of gypsies, children, and women in the Maxwell Street neighborhood.

Title: City views
Description: Views of Chicago (Ill.) including exterior views of the Art Institute, Lincoln Park Zoo, and vendor booths on Maxwell Street, photographed for Wilfred Floing.

Title: Jerome Joseph photograph collection
Description: Photographs of the Maxwell Street Market area taken by Jerome Joseph while he was a student at the Illinois Institute of Technology in 1950-1951. Images include views of the streets and crowds as well as individual vendors and shoppers.

Title: Raymond Kastle Chicago slides, 1960-1972.
Description: Color 35mm slides of Chicago buildings, street scenes, and events taken by amateur photographer Raymond Kastle. Street scenes focus on North Loop, Near North, and Maxwell Street areas and include images of Marina City towers and along the Chicago River, notably boats unloading at the Chicago Sun-Times Building. Events include the 1968 Auto Show and two Japanese festivals, the Oban Festival and Ginza Days (1961). Also included are images of White Sox Comiskey Park and several unidentified team players (1968).

Title: Edward Fisher photograph collection
Description: Exterior views of the Maxwell Street Market area taken by Edward Fisher, amateur photographer and frequent visitor to the market. Images show unidentified merchants working the market, customers, and buildings and other structures, both in the market and the surrounding area.

Title: Changing Chicago project photographs by Jay Wolke
Description: Documentary photographs of Chicago's Maxwell Street Market district, an open-air flea market. Includes images of shoppers, pedestrians, vendors, peddlers, street musicians, and events. Photographs show primarily African American and Hispanic American people.

Title: Ron Gordon visual materials 1971-2016.
Description: Black-and-white photographic negatives (approximately 780, 8 in. x 10 in. and smaller), 20 in. x 24 in. photographic prints (2,308), 4 in. x 5 in. photographic prints (5,195), and contact sheets (approximately 274); 8 in. x 10 in. color prints (6); and color transparencies (112, 4 in. x 5 in. and smaller) by Ron Gordon related to his professional work as a freelance photographer in Chicago. Images document Chicago<U+2019>s built environment and building demolitions over the last decades of the twentieth century (primarily South Loop, Pilsen, and Bronzeville neighborhoods and residents), projects like Sculpture Chicago and "Changing Chicago," baseball games at Comiskey Park, and airplanes in flight near Midway Airport. Images also include photographs published in Arcadia Publishing<U+2019>s "Forgotten Chicago" and "Printers Row, Chicago." Other photographic material relating to named projects and assignments include Gordon<U+2019>s published work for the "Chicago Reader" and the Mexican publication, "Travesias." Also included is published and printed material related to these projects.

Title: Beatrijs Kuyck-Hechtermans photograph collection
Description: Images made by Kuyck-Hechtermans while she was a graduate student at the Institute of Design in Chicago (Ill.), including architectural views. Topics include Maxwell Street, Mies van der Rohe's 860 N. Lake Shore Drive apartment buildings, the Chicago River, Lincoln Park, Lake Shore Drive, lakefront activities, street scenes, children, an ice skating show at the Boulevard Room in 1951, and Ravinia Park in Highland Park (Ill.).

Title: [Florence Carsello, bombing victim, sitting on knee of Martin Ernest, policeman]
Description: Half-length portrait of Florence Carsello, a bombing victim, sitting on the knee of Martin Ernest, policeman from the Maxwell Street Station. An unidentified boy is sitting in the background. Florence's family was the target of a bomb explosion in their home at 846 South Miller Street. in the Near West Side community area of Chicago, Illinois. Florence had been buried under the debris, but was rescued by police detectives. The rest of the family also survived with minimum injuries.

Title: Frank M. Getchel slide collection, [ca. 1940-1949].
Description: Views of Chicago by amateur photographer Getchel, including Buckingham Fountain, the Chicago Board of Trade building, the Chicago River, the Conrad Hilton Hotel, Field Museum of Natural History, gypsies on Maxwell Street, Michigan Avenue, Midway Airport, North Avenue Beach with bathers, the Railroad Fair of 1948, Union Station, and various streetscapes, buildings, car parks and panoramic views.

Title: Chicago Journal photograph collection
Description: Photographs from The Chicago Journal: The South Side's Free Newsweekly, a neighborhood newspaper. Includes images of Chicago's south side, such as residential streets, public housing, and businesses. Includes images of the Pullman and Douglas communities. Many photographs show people, often involved in some activity. People include politicians, entertainers, activists, and educators among others. Most images relate to newsworthy events, such as social events, crimes, demonstrations, and political activities. Some photographs show police at work. One box of photographs shows African Americans and relate to racial discrimination. Some African Americans are entertainers or performing artists. Also includes material on recycling garbage, sports, streets (notably, the Maxwell Street market), and transportation.

Title: Lenora Linson photograph collection
Description: Photographs by Lenora Linson, a Wisconsin native who resided in Chicago while a nurse at Cook County Hospital, located on Chicago's Near West Side. Images include nurses and doctors of Cook County Hospital on duty, live birth scenes, hospital equipment in use, hospital interiors, the Cook County School of Nursing Dormitory interiors and exteriors, Cook County School of Nursing library interior, West Side building exteriors, Maxwell Street Market scenes, Soldier Field in 1941, and miscellaneous Chicago neighborhood scenes. The collection features nurses in various uniforms at work and at leisure, and include candid photographs of nursing students in the dormitory and neighborhood. Also present are numerous personal photographs of the Linson family, friends, and sightseeing at such locations and sites as Washington, D.C.; Colorado; desert; camping; and nature.

Title: Sigmund J. Osty visual materials, approximately 1960-1976
Description: Black-and-white photographic prints depicting the built environment, predominantly in Chicago, but also Evanston, Skokie, and Galena, Illinois. All the images depict exterior views, the majority of which are street intersections, though the collection also documents streetscapes, residences, and individual businesses, particularly churches, department stores, and burlesque and pornographic film establishments. Osty most frequently documented the River North, Near North Side, Cabrini-Green, Gold Coast, and Old Town areas (bounded by Menomonee (1800 North) to the Chicago River (300 North), Lake Michigan to Halsted St. (800 West)); the collection also includes many images (approximately 300) of the Downtown Chicago area (bounded by the Chicago River (300 North) to Harrison St. (600 South), Michigan Avenue (100 East) to I-90/94 Expressway (700 West)). Other areas documented include the Lakefront and Museum Campus, South Loop and Chinatown, South Commons, Bronzeville, Hyde Park, Englewood, Bridgeport and New City, Homan Square, the West Loop and Near West Side, Garfield Park, University Village/Maxwell Street, Little Italy, Illinois Medical District, Pilsen, River West, Goose Island, Noble Square, West Town, Ukrainian Village, Wicker Park, Bucktown, Logan Square, Humboldt Park, Jefferson Park, Portage Park, Lincoln Park, Lakeview, West Lakeview, North Center and Lincoln Square, Uptown, Edgewater, Rogers Park and Andersonville. The collection includes images of the Maxwell Street markets, the original Hull House and its relocation, and a number of images taken from the observation deck in the John Hancock Center. Some of the images were taken for camera club presentations or competitions, and nearly all images have been labeled by Osty with either an address or cross-streets and the month/year.

Title: Ron Popeil photograph collection
Description: Includes photographs of the Chicago inventor and businessman Ron Popeil with his products such as the Food Dehydrator.

Title: Art Shay photograph collection 1944-2002.
Description: The collection includes a wide variety of images depicting people in Chicago neighborhoods (such as Maxwell Street Market and a skid row along Madison Street), celebrities in Chicago and elsewhere, entertainers, politicians, gamblers, prisoners, authors, and other cultural symbols. Many images qualify as Art Shay<U+2019>s famous "one-liners," in which one photograph combines unlikely and disparate elements and perhaps a caption to create multiple meanings within the same frame.

Title: Chicago Maternity Center photograph collection
Description: Includes photographs relating to the Chicago Maternity Center, a home-childbirth service and pre-natal clinic in the Maxwell Street area of the Near West Side of Chicago (Ill.). This center probably was associated with the Chicago Lying-in Hospital. Includes portraits of Dr. J.B. DeLee, Dr. Frank Rubovits, Dr. Beatrice Tucker, and other staff.

Title: Newberry Avenue Center photograph collection
Description: Photographs of activities and classes at the Newberry Avenue Center, located at the corner of Maxwell Street and Newberry Avenue in the Near West Side of Chicago (Ill.), including boxing, sewing, cooking, playing, storytelling, reading, English language instruction, health clinic, and playtime.

Title: Documentary photographs by students at University of Illinois at Chicago
Description: Photographs submitted for Art & Design course 269 taught by Robert Stiegler at UIC, Spring 1986. Photographs primarily show street scenes in residential areas, focusing on Bridgeport, Lakeview and Pilsen communities. Some photographs depict small businesses or restaurants and their owners. Others show residents, schools, grocery stores, interiors of loft apartments, Wrigley (baseball) Field and lakefront scenes. A few photographs show campaign materials for Harold Washington/Bernard Epton mayoralty election. One series has scenes from Maxwell Street and South Water Street market areas. Afrrican Americans and Hispanic Americans are depicted.
Photographer: Steigler, Robert.; University of Illinois at Chicago

Title: Mildred Mead photograph collection
Description: Photographs, nearly all by Mildred Mead, a photographer for the Metropolitan Housing and Planning Council, showing neighborhoods in Chicago (Ill.) targeted by the Metropolitan Housing and Planning Council for urban renewal. The photographs depict slum conditions, homes in revitalized areas (including homes operated by the Chicago Housing Authority), and other aspects of community life in Chicago, including churches and parishioners, schools, street markets, parades, road construction, newly integrated communities, and children at play. Community areas represented by many images in the collection include: Englewood, Hyde Park, Kenwood, Near West Side, Near North Side, and New City. Market streets areas include Fulton Street Market (fish), Randolph Street Market, South Water Market (produce), Wood Street Terminal "Potato Yard," Maxwell Street Market and nearby areas.
